items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There’s Red Holloway, Teddy Edwards. There’s some great guys around here that they’re stylists, that have a good sound.

ctx.x: I knew Rickey Henderson was versatile but I didn’t know it extended into music.

No, I just said that because I like to mention people that are making millions of dollars because I don’t think musicians get in that bracket. But Rickey’s a great tenor player. There’s Red Holloway, Teddy Edwards. There’s some great guys around here that they’re stylists, that have a good sound. I just think that the business has gotten to the point where it’s just a matter of how much money am I going to make. A lot of guys … and the youngsters now, they make so much money. They make more in three months than I…

Do you feel any, not resentment, but just the irony of something like Columbia seeming to sign every young musician almost on the basis of youth. It seems that you have to be under 25, even if they’re of marginal talent but just the fact that they’re young and can play, I mean it’s not that they’re completely incompetent but they all sound alike, do you sort of resent the attention that’s been focused on this younger movement in jazz?

items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: I was up in Canada with Sweets Edison, and Sonny Payne was with us

ctx.x: of things with the drumsticks; all kind of things. In fact, later, a few years ago, I was up in Canada with Sweets Edison, and Sonny Payne was with us, and he was doing his tricks with the drumsticks, you know. And he said to me, "I bet you don't know where I got that from." I said, "I'll betcha I do!" [LAUGHS HEARTILY] And he said, "Lionel Hampton?" -- because Hampton was famous for doing it. But they all got it from Kid Lips, you know. I said, "No, you got that from Kid Lips Hackett." That blew his mind, that I…

And that band used to parade also. But they were more classy than Rabbit Foot. In fact, Louis Jordan came out of that band with Old Man Joe White on the Rabbit Foot Minstrel Show. That's right. They brought Louis Jordan out of Brinkley, Arkansas. That was his first outing, was with the Rabbit Foot Minstrel Show Band. They were stationed down at Fort Gibson, but they'd come to Jackson and play. Their home base was in Fort Gibson, Mississippi. And Silas Green's home base was in Brumley(?), Georgia.
